findings: Both snapshots describe Radar using network data and hundreds of risk factors to determine each payment's risk score and level and help decide when to block or send to review. The merchant can open Show all insights. Both say data is retained for up to six months and that older transactions cannot open the interface.

Both say integration-provided email, IP and shipping help Radar compute the available data. Risk insights can show name/email correspondence, transactions' authorization rate on Stripe network associated with the email, and billing/shipping/IP geography. A low rate only might indicate suspicion, because past declines sometimes suggest fraud attempts.

Both dedicated Risk Insights pins say Related Payments includes the merchant's own other payments sharing customer ID, IP, or card number. Many cards sharing one IP or customers sharing a card are possible investigative signals, not fraud verdicts.
substantive_changes: November abbreviates the eligibility and fraud-factor documentation. It omits the earlier Fraud Teams availability attribution, the detailed numbers and Top Fraud Factors sections, hover distribution context and the sandbox statement. Preserve the May scope as historical evidence. Omission establishes no rollout or feature removal.
November still routes users to Show all insights, moved higher on the page, and retains the six-month risk-insights interface restriction.
historical_claims_to_preserve: May 10 states availability with Radar for Fraud Teams and describes fraud factor numbers and top factors with a preceding scope of charges within the last six months and no support for payments in sandboxes. Keep that scope tied to the May fraud-factor passage, rather than asserting a current blanket sandbox restriction for all Risk Insights.

May explains numerical factors as comparative charge likelihood for similar values versus the Stripe average. High-risk charges are expected to have some factors above 1 and low-risk charges some below 1. It describes possible changes over time and says a fraud decision can follow from a combination without individually suspicious factors.
conflicts: The summary says Fraud Teams only, no sandbox, and high/low factors as categorical conclusions, and equates low authorization rate with suspicious behavior. Narrow these to the May availability and sandbox evidence, and retain probability wording from both captures.

The dedicated Risk Insights guide says customer ID/IP/card while the November transaction reviews guide says email/IP/card for its linked Related Payments text. Preserve both formulations separately and avoid inferring an exhaustive union or treating customer ID as email.
